case_name: State Of Rajasthan And Anr. v Shantilal Etc.
respondent:
Shantilal Etc.
Supreme Court of India

2 August 1989
Civil Appeal Nos. 6 147-6 148 of 1983
The Judgment was delivered by: Kuldip Singh, J.
1.  The question for consideration in these two appeals is whether the creation of two cadres, consisting of Nursing Superintendent Grade I, Nursing Superintendent Grade II, Assistant Nursing Superintendent and Nursing Tutor (hereinafter called 'nursing cadre') and of Compounder Grade I, Compounder Grade 1I and Compounder Grade III (hereinafter called 'compounders cadre') under the Rajasthan Medical and Health Subordinate Service Rules, 1965 (hereinafter called 'Rules'), is arbitrary and as such violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
The relevant facts are as under.

facts: Bansi Lal Sharma was appointed as Male Nurse in 1941.
He qualified Punjab Nursing Registration Council Examination in 1944 and was confirmed as Compounder Grade-I in 1950.
He was officiating as Sister Tutor when the rules came into force in March, 1966.
He filed writ petition in the Rajasthan High Court in 1971 challenging the creation of two separate cadres under the rules.
Kan Singh, J. rejected the contentions of Sharma and held that there was no arbitrariness in creating two separate cadres for nurses and compounders.
Shanti Lal Jain, in the second case, was appointed compounder Grade-IV in 1955.
He was confirmed as compounder Grade-I in the year 1959 and in March, 1966 when the rules were enforced, he was holding the post of Sister Tutor on officiating basis.
He also challenged the vires of the rules on the grounds of Articles 14, 15 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
issues: Whether the creation of two cadres is arbitrary and violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
Whether the rules are constitutionally valid.
petitioner_arguments: The creation of two separate cadres under the rules has arbitrarily deprived compounders Grade-I of their right to promotion to the higher posts of Assistant Nursing Superintendent, Nursing Superintendent Grade-II and Nursing Superintendent Grade-I.
Recruitment to the nursing cadre was confined to females alone which resulted in discrimination on the ground of sex and as such violative of Art. 15 of the Constitution of India.
respondent_arguments: There was no arbitrariness in creating two separate cadres for nurses and compounders.
The creation of two separate cadres did not infringe the equality clause and also that there was no discrimination on the ground of sex.
court_reasoning: The creation of cadres in the service of the State is a matter which has to be left entirely to the State Government.
Arts. 14 and 16 do not forbid the creation of different cadres for government service, nor do they prevent the integration of different cadres into one cadre.

The High Court's reasoning that nurses and compounders form one class and as such treating them differently by creating two separate cadres is discriminatory and violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India was strained and incorrect.
holding: We accept the appeals and set aside the judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court.
Affirming the judgments of the learned single Judges we hold that the rules are constitutionally valid.
There shall be no order as to costs.
